title: The Giant Three-Point Jump
premise: An announcer wants an honest chart of scores 97 and 100, but a cropped vertical axis makes the change look enormous. Restoring a labeled zero baseline and displaying the difference lets the audience compare both views.
hook: Did the score triple, or did the camera move?
visible_action: A bar-chart camera pulls back to expose the hidden axis range while numeric labels remain fixed.
intended_takeaway_or_theme: Chart scale can change visual emphasis without changing the numbers.
gate: Explain that a nonzero axis is not automatically dishonest; context and labeling matter.

editorial_pick.original_reason: A truncated chart can produce a strong before/after reveal without a large scene.
editorial_pick.proposed_first_version: Show the exact same three data points with two clearly labeled axis ranges, then inspect the apparent difference.
editorial_pick.gate: Use explicitly illustrative data, preserve the values and label axes. Do not manufacture an empirical claim.
